title: Clock Mode State Machine
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Clocks and Watches with AI
description: A three-state clock (RUN, SET_HOUR, SET_MINUTE) driven by Mode and Cycle buttons, with a mock display, clickable state descriptions and a predict-the-next-state mode.

learningObjectives: Apply a state machine to predict what a Mode press does in each state
Predict what a Cycle press does to the hour and minute in each state
Explain why the same button can mean different things in different states
prerequisites: Buttons and interrupts from earlier in this chapter

accessibility.notes: Controls are standard HTML form elements

keyQuestions: How many Mode presses bring you back to RUN?
What does Cycle do in RUN, and why is that useful?
What line of code moves to the next state?
commonMisconceptions: Each button always does the same thing
Mode can go backward to the previous state
Pressing Cycle in SET_MINUTE also changes the hour when minutes wrap
assessmentOpportunities: Students predict the next state correctly every time in Predict mode.
Students set a requested time with the fewest presses.
Students extend the diagram to five states and change % 3 to % 5.

controls.label: Cycle
controls.description: Adds 1 to the hour or minute in a setting state

controls.label: Predict
controls.description: Asks for the next state before it moves
